2027-05-31.title: The Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
readings: The King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst
Great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel
Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
2027-05-31.alt: Feast. Gloria; no Creed. The readings are proper to the feast and replace those of Monday of the Ninth Week in Ordinary Time. Either Zephaniah 3:14–18a or Romans 12:9–16 may be read as the first reading; the responsorial psalm is the canticle of Isaiah 12. Since 1969 the Visitation is kept on 31 May, between the Annunciation (25 March) and the Birth of St John the Baptist (24 June); it closes the month of May, dedicated to Mary. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-05-31.verse: And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
theo: On the last day of the month of Mary the Church follows a young woman on a journey. The prophet Zephaniah, writing in a dark time for Jerusalem, suddenly breaks into a song of joy addressed to “daughter Zion”: “Sing aloud, O daughter Zion; shout, O Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, O daughter Jerusalem!” The reason for the joy is a presence: “The king of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you shall fear disaster no more.” And again: “Do not fear, O Zion; do not let your hands grow weak. The LORD, your God, is in your midst, a warrior who gives victory; he will rejoice over you with gladness, he will renew you in his love; he will exult over you with loud singing as on a day of festival.” The Hebrew for “in your midst” can also mean “within you,” “in your womb.” The Church has always heard in these words the voice of the angel to Mary: “Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you” (Luke 1:28), a greeting that in Greek begins with the word “Rejoice,” and then: do not be afraid. Mary is the true daughter Zion, and the Lord is now, literally, within her. The responsorial psalm, the song of Isaiah 12, carries the same joy: “Shout aloud and sing for joy, O royal Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.” Where the second option is read, St Paul's words in Romans 12 sound like a portrait of what Mary does in today's Gospel: “Let love be genuine,” “extend hospitality to strangers,” “Rejoice with those who rejoice,” “do not be haughty, but associate with the lowly.”

Then the Gospel. Mary has just heard the angel's message, and has heard too that her elderly relative Elizabeth, “who was said to be barren,” is in her sixth month. Her first response to the gift of God is not to stay at home and wonder, but to go and serve: “In those days Mary set out and went with haste to a Judean town in the hill country.” It was a journey of perhaps four days on foot, from Nazareth in the north to the hills near Jerusalem, where tradition places the village of Ein Karem. Mary carries the Son of God within her, hidden and very small, and she brings him to another home. St Luke tells the story with words that echo the Old Testament account of the Ark of the Covenant being brought into the hill country of Judah (2 Samuel 6). There, David asked in awe, “How can the ark of the LORD come into my care?”; here Elizabeth asks, “And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?” There, David leaped and danced before the ark; here, “the child leaped in her womb.” There, the ark stayed three months in the house of Obed-edom and brought blessing; here, “Mary remained with her about three months.” Mary is the new Ark, carrying not the tablets of the Law but the Word made flesh.

Elizabeth, “filled with the Holy Spirit,” speaks the words that the Church repeats millions of times a day in the Hail Mary: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” She calls Mary “the mother of my Lord,” the first time in St Luke's Gospel that a human voice calls Jesus Lord, and the basis of the Church's faith that Mary is truly the Mother of God (Catechism 495). And she praises Mary's faith: “blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.” Then Mary sings. The Magnificat is woven out of the Psalms and the song of Hannah (1 Samuel 2), the prayer of a young woman who knew the Scriptures by heart. “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant.” She does not boast of herself; she boasts of God, who “has done great things for me.” And then the song widens to the whole of history: God “has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly; he has filled the hungry with good things, and sent the rich away empty.” The God who chose a poor girl from Nazareth is the God who takes the side of the poor. Every evening, at Vespers, the Church sings this song with Mary. On this last day of May we may ask her for two gifts: her haste to serve, and her joy in God.
conn: A poetic title for Jerusalem and the people of God (Zephaniah 3:14; Zechariah 9:9). The Church sees in Mary the true daughter Zion, in whom God comes to dwell (Catechism 722).
Hebrew beqirbek, used twice in Zephaniah 3:15, 17; it can also mean “within you,” even “in your womb.” Many scholars hear an echo of it in the angel's greeting to Mary in Luke 1:28–31.
Greek meta spoudes: with eagerness, with zeal. Mary's haste is not anxiety but the readiness of love. St Ambrose wrote that the grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow efforts (in substance).
Tradition identifies Elizabeth's town with Ein Karem, about seven kilometres west of Jerusalem, where two churches recall the Visitation and the birth of John.

Luke's account echoes 2 Samuel 6: the ark goes up to the hill country of Judah, David asks how it can come to him, he leaps before it, and it remains three months. Mary carries the Word of God made flesh (Catechism 2676).
The same verb (skirtao) is used of joyful leaping. John begins his mission of pointing to Christ before he is born; the Church sees him sanctified by the presence of the Lord (Catechism 717, 523).
In the Greek Old Testament “Lord” (Kyrios) translates the divine name. Elizabeth's words are a root of the title Mother of God (Theotokos), defined at the Council of Ephesus in 431 (Catechism 495).
Mary's song, named from its first word in Latin. It echoes the song of Hannah (1 Samuel 2:1–10) and many psalms, and is sung every day at Evening Prayer (Catechism 2619).

The Visitation was spread by the Franciscans in the thirteenth century and extended to the whole Church in 1389, on 2 July. The calendar reform of 1969 placed it on 31 May, between the Annunciation and the Birth of John the Baptist (St Paul VI, Marialis Cultus 7).
altar: Mary carried the hidden Christ to Elizabeth's house, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaped for joy. At this altar the same Lord comes hidden under the appearance of bread and wine, truly present, Body and Blood, soul and divinity. When we receive him, we too become bearers of Christ, sent out with haste to the homes of others.

Every Mass is a visitation: God comes to his people. With Elizabeth we may say before Communion, why has this happened to me, that my Lord comes to me? and with Mary, after Communion, my soul magnifies the Lord.
outline: Ask: when God gives you a great joy, what is the first thing you do with it?
The Lord in your midst: Zephaniah's joy fulfilled in Mary.
Point 2 · With haste to the hill country
Mary carries Christ to serve; the new Ark of the Covenant.
Point 3 · Blessed is she who believed
Elizabeth, filled with the Spirit, greets the Mother of the Lord.
Point 4 · My soul magnifies the Lord
Mary's song of the lowly lifted up and the hungry filled.
Two expectant mothers embracing in a doorway in the hills, and an unborn child leaping for joy.
live: This week visit an elderly relative, a pregnant mother, or a neighbour who is alone, as Mary visited Elizabeth, and offer practical help.
Pray Luke 1:46–55 slowly each evening this week, as the Church does at Vespers.
End the Marian month today by praying the Rosary as a family, the Joyful Mysteries if you can, and thanking Mary for her care.
When you see a need today, do not delay: act on it at once, with joy.
fathers: Mary went with haste into the hill country, not because she doubted the angel, but because she rejoiced in the promise and was eager to serve. The grace of the Holy Spirit knows no slow efforts.

Let the soul of Mary be in each of us to magnify the Lord; let the spirit of Mary be in each of us to rejoice in God. If according to the flesh there is one mother of Christ, according to faith Christ is the fruit of all.

It is a good and holy custom in the Church that this hymn of the Mother of God is sung every day at the evening office, so that the remembrance of the Lord's Incarnation may kindle the devotion of the faithful.
magis: Mary, called in the Gospels “the mother of Jesus,” is acclaimed by Elizabeth as “the mother of my Lord”; she is truly Mother of God (Theotokos).
The Virgin Mary most perfectly embodies the obedience of faith; Elizabeth greets her: “blessed is she who believed.”
John the Baptist, filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb, rejoices at the coming of Christ.
The Magnificat is the song both of the Mother of God and of the Church.
The words of the Hail Mary come from the angel's greeting and Elizabeth's blessing; Mary is the Ark of the Covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells.
saints: The feast was first kept by the Franciscans, encouraged by St Bonaventure in 1263, and extended to the whole Latin Church by Pope Urban VI in 1389. It gives its name to the Order of the Visitation, founded in 1610 by St Francis de Sales and St Jane Frances de Chantal to unite prayer with gentle service.

Elizabeth, of the priestly family of Aaron, and her husband Zechariah were “righteous before God” (Luke 1:6). Filled with the Holy Spirit, she was the first to call Mary the mother of the Lord. Both are honoured as saints in the Roman Martyrology.
2027-05-31.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, who, while the Blessed Virgin Mary was carrying your Son in her womb, inspired her to visit Elizabeth, grant us, we pray, that, faithful to the promptings of the Spirit, we may magnify your greatness with the Virgin Mary at all times. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you went with haste to serve, carrying Christ within you. Teach us your joy and your readiness. As this month of May ends, take our families under your care, and help us to bring Jesus to every home we enter. Amen.

quick: Zephaniah calls daughter Zion to rejoice because the Lord, the King of Israel, is in her midst.
Carrying Jesus in her womb, Mary goes with haste to serve Elizabeth, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy.
Elizabeth blesses Mary as the mother of my Lord, and Mary sings the Magnificat: my soul magnifies the Lord.
2027-05-31.action: Visit or call someone who needs help this week, and do it promptly and joyfully.
2027-05-31.question: Do I carry Jesus to others, or keep my faith to myself?
catechism: Mary is truly the Mother of God.
The Magnificat, song of Mary and of the Church.
The Hail Mary and Mary as the Ark of the Covenant.
kidsaint: Elizabeth was Mary's relative. She and her husband Zechariah had waited many, many years for a baby, and now, when they were old, God gave them a son, John the Baptist! When Mary came to visit, Elizabeth felt her baby jump for joy inside her, and she knew at once that Mary was carrying Jesus. She said to Mary: blessed are you among women! We still say her words every time we pray the Hail Mary. Lesson: God sees those who wait patiently, and he fills them with joy.
2027-05-31.special: Feast of the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Gloria; no Creed. Proper readings: Zephaniah 3:14–18a or Romans 12:9–16; Isaiah 12; Luke 1:39–56. Close of the month of May.
term: The song of Mary in Luke 1:46–55, named from its first word in Latin, Magnificat anima mea Dominum, my soul magnifies the Lord. It praises God who lifts up the lowly and fills the hungry, and is sung every evening at Vespers, the Evening Prayer of the Church.

family.explain: After the angel's visit, Mary heard that her old relative Elizabeth was going to have a baby. Mary did not wait; she hurried over the hills to help her. When Mary said hello, the baby inside Elizabeth jumped for joy, because Jesus was inside Mary! Elizabeth said: blessed are you among women! Mary stayed three months to help her.
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are expecting a baby, for elderly people who need help, and for all who serve the sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we visit or help this week, the way Mary helped Elizabeth?” End the month of May by praying the Rosary together tonight.

illus: In a hill village in Idukki a young mother in the last months of her own pregnancy heard that her elderly neighbour had fallen and could not leave her bed. Her family told her to rest. Instead she went every morning, slowly, up the steep path with a flask of kanji and a clean towel, and sat with the old woman, praying the Rosary with her. The neighbour said afterwards: when she came through the door, I felt as if Our Lady herself had come in. That is what the Visitation looks like in our hills. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who filled Elizabeth and moved Mary to go with haste, fill us now with joy and readiness to serve. With Mary we say: my soul magnifies the Lord. Amen.
share: The Lord, your God, is in your midst (Zephaniah 3:17). Do I live with the joy of one in whom God dwells?
Mary set out and went with haste (Luke 1:39). Is there a visit or a service I keep putting off?
He has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant (Luke 1:48). Where has God lifted me up when I felt small?
pm.resp: Great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may go out in haste to serve the poor and the forgotten.
For expectant mothers, especially those who are alone or afraid, and for their unborn children.
For the elderly and housebound, that they may be visited and cared for.
For the hungry and the lowly, that the Lord may fill them with good things through our generosity.
For our group, that we may carry Christ to every home we enter, as Mary did.
pm.close: Father, you inspired the Virgin Mary to visit Elizabeth. Make us attentive to the Spirit and ready to serve, that with Mary we may magnify your name for ever. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we close the month of May with a beautiful journey. A young woman from Nazareth, who has just said yes to God, sets out on foot over the hills. She is carrying the Son of God within her. Nobody can see him yet. But wherever she goes, he goes.

The prophet Zephaniah had sung long before: sing aloud, O daughter Zion! The Lord, your God, is in your midst (Zephaniah 3:14, 17). The Hebrew words can mean in your womb. In Mary the prophecy is fulfilled literally. God is not only near his people; he is living inside a young girl from a small village. That is why Mary's whole life is joy.

And what does she do with this joy? St Luke says: Mary set out and went with haste (Luke 1:39). She does not stay at home thinking about her privilege. She hears that her old relative Elizabeth is expecting a baby, and she goes to help. The first thing Mary does with Jesus is to carry him to someone in need. That is the pattern for every Christian: the one who receives Jesus goes out to serve.

When Mary greets her, Elizabeth's child leaps for joy, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. She cries out: blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me? (Luke 1:42–43). Every time we pray the Hail Mary, we repeat Elizabeth's words. And she adds: blessed is she who believed. Mary's greatness is first her faith.

Then Mary sings: my soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior (Luke 1:46–47). She sings of a God who looks at the lowly, who brings down the powerful and lifts up the humble, who fills the hungry with good things. Mary is not proud. She is happy because God is great and God is good to the poor. If we want to honour Mary, we must also care for the lowly and the hungry.

Today let us thank Mary for this month of May, for every Rosary prayed in our homes. And let us ask her for her haste: when we see someone in need, let us not delay. Let us visit the sick, the old, the lonely, the expectant mother. Let us carry Jesus to them, as Mary did. And then, with her, our souls too will magnify the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, after the angel told Mary she would be the mother of Jesus, she heard that her cousin Elizabeth was going to have a baby too. Did Mary say, I am too important now? No! She ran over the hills to help Elizabeth. And when Mary said hello, the baby inside Elizabeth jumped for joy, because baby Jesus was inside Mary!
Today is the last day of May, Mary's month. Let us be like Mary. Is there someone at home you can help today, quickly and with a smile? Then you are bringing Jesus to them, just like Mary did.

intro: The joy of daughter Zion, the haste of love, the faith that Elizabeth praised, and the song of the lowly lifted up.

concl: In Mary the Lord is truly in the midst of his people; she carries him with haste to serve.
Elizabeth praises her faith, and Mary sings of the God who lifts up the lowly; we close the month of May by learning her joy and her readiness.
2027-05-31.resolve: Pray the Magnificat each evening this week and make one visit of service, as Mary did.
